caveats.message: A stable event-derived fingerprint is evidence of individual signal, not proof of playing style.
Same-season club continuity is a strong confound and can make identity retrieval easier.
Transferred-player evidence is based on a small sample and has wide uncertainty.
The independent-provider replication is positive but lower in magnitude than the Wyscout result.

experiments.conclusion: The 32-feature fingerprint retrieves the same player far better than the role-and-minutes baseline.
experiments.title: Wyscout global same-player retrieval

experiments.conclusion: The signal remains when nominal role can no longer resolve the retrieval problem.
experiments.population: 1,257 eligible units with candidates restricted to nominal role
experiments.title: Wyscout within-role retrieval

experiments.conclusion: Team continuity is a stronger shortcut than the fingerprint in this same-season design.
experiments.title: Role + team + minutes control

experiments.conclusion: The Wyscout fingerprint remains encouraging after a team change, but the sample is small.
experiments.population: 26 players who changed team between periods
experiments.title: Wyscout transferred-player stress test

experiments.conclusion: The fingerprint signal replicates with a different provider and season at a lower magnitude.
experiments.title: StatsBomb global replication

experiments.conclusion: The cross-provider signal is not explained only by nominal role.
experiments.population: 1,061 eligible units with candidates restricted to role
experiments.title: StatsBomb within-role replication

experiments.conclusion: The transferred-player effect is inconclusive in the smaller StatsBomb sample.
experiments.title: StatsBomb transferred-player stress test

experiments.conclusion: Shrinkage reduced low-support ratio extremes but did not improve retrieval, so raw ratios remain the default.
experiments.title: Raw versus shrunk ratio features

narrative_steps.summary: Freeze a chronological same-player retrieval task before reading the result.
narrative_steps.title: Can an event profile identify a player?

narrative_steps.summary: The 32-feature cosine model materially exceeds the role-and-minutes baseline.
narrative_steps.title: A strong temporal fingerprint appears

narrative_steps.summary: A role, team, and minutes control outperforms the fingerprint and narrows the interpretation.
narrative_steps.title: Team continuity is a powerful shortcut

narrative_steps.summary: The Wyscout signal survives the shortcut removal, with wide uncertainty from a small sample.
narrative_steps.title: Stress-test players who changed team

narrative_steps.summary: StatsBomb independently reproduces the core signal at a lower magnitude; its transfer subset is inconclusive.
narrative_steps.title: Repeat with another provider

narrative_steps.summary: Ratio shrinkage fixes a local pathology but does not improve retrieval, so it is not promoted.
narrative_steps.title: Keep a useful correction out when it does not help

supported_claim: Event-derived profiles contain a reproducible individual fingerprint that supports same-player temporal retrieval across two chronological halves.
unsupported_claims: A statistical neighbor is a recruitment recommendation or replacement.
The experiment predicts future performance, tactical fit, value, or transfer success.
